# mtncloud_load_balancer_health_monitor (Resource)

The health check of a load balancer pool: members that fail it get no traffic until they pass again. A pool has at most one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "mtncloud_load_balancer" "web" {
  network_id = mtncloud_network.app.id
  name       = "web"
}

resource "mtncloud_load_balancer_pool" "web" {
  network_id       = mtncloud_network.app.id
  load_balancer_id = mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id
  protocol         = "HTTP"
  algorithm        = "ROUND_ROBIN"
}

resource "mtncloud_load_balancer_health_monitor" "web" {
  network_id       = mtncloud_network.app.id
  load_balancer_id = mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id
  pool_id          = mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.web.id
  type             = "HTTP"
  delay            = 5
  timeout          = 3
  max_retries      = 3
  url_path         = "/health"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `delay` (Number) Seconds between checks.
- `load_balancer_id` (String) ID of the load balancer, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer.web.id`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `max_retries` (Number) Passed checks in a row before a member counts as up, 1 to 10.
- `network_id` (Number) ID of the MTN Network the load balancer is on, for example `mtncloud_network.app.id`. Your tenant must own it: a network shared with you is read-only. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `pool_id` (String) The pool it checks, for example `mtncloud_load_balancer_pool.web.id`. Changing it replaces the health monitor.
- `timeout` (Number) Seconds to wait for an answer. Must be less than `delay`.
- `type` (String) `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, `PING`, `TCP`, `TLS-HELLO`, `UDP-CONNECT` or `SCTP`. Changing it replaces the health monitor.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the health monitor takes traffic (administrative state). Defaults to `true`.
- `expected_codes` (String) The status codes that count as healthy: `200`, `200,202` or `200-204`. For `HTTP` and `HTTPS` checks. Taken out of the configuration, it keeps its last value.
- `http_method` (String) The request method: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `TRACE`, `OPTIONS`, `PATCH` or `CONNECT`. For `HTTP` and `HTTPS` checks. Taken out of the configuration, it keeps its last value.
- `max_retries_down` (Number) Failed checks in a row before a member counts as down, 1 to 10. Taken out of the configuration, it keeps its last value.
- `name` (String) The health monitor's name.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `url_path` (String) The path requested, for example `/health`. For `HTTP` and `HTTPS` checks. Taken out of the configuration, it keeps its last value.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The health monitor's ID.

- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A pool has at most one health monitor, so it is imported by its pool.
terraform import mtncloud_load_balancer_health_monitor.web <network_id>/<load_balancer_id>/<pool_id>
```
